workflow: Follow a strict 3-phase workflow: (1) LOCATE phase (3-4 commands max): use grep to search for error messages/function names, use git log/blame to find recent changes, use find/ls to locate relevant files - stop searching once you identify the likely buggy file; (2) UNDERSTAND phase (5-7 commands max): read the specific file with cat or nl, view exact line numbers using 'nl -ba filename | sed -n "start,end p"', identify the EXACT lines needing change, verify line numbers before proceeding; (3) FIX phase (remaining budget): make surgical edits using sed with specific line numbers (e.g., 'sed -i "42s/old/new/" file'), verify each edit immediately with git diff to confirm only intended lines changed, run tests to validate the fix, iterate if tests fail. Label each step with its phase in your reasoning. After 25 steps total, prioritize completing a fix over perfect understanding.
context_strategy: Keep conversation history focused on the current phase. In LOCATE, track which search patterns succeeded or failed to avoid repeating ineffective greps. In UNDERSTAND, retain the exact line numbers and content you identified - line numbers shift after edits so re-verify before each edit operation. In FIX, maintain a record of what you've already edited via git diff output to avoid duplicate or conflicting changes. If you hit a format error (multiple actions in one response), immediately simplify to exactly one bash command block per turn - this is the #1 self-inflicted failure mode. Discard verbose command templates or scaffolding that bloat the context without improving accuracy.
submission_strategy: Before submitting, verify: (1) you have made at least one concrete code edit (checked via git diff showing actual line changes), (2) you are in the FIX phase (not still searching or reading), (3) if possible, you have run the relevant tests and seen improvement (but do NOT author your own tests or use git checkout to revert code as validation - only trust pre-existing test commands from the repo). Never submit after only running a one-line reproduction script or after restoring/reverting files with git checkout. Never batch the submission command with other commands (pytest + git diff + COMPLETE_TASK in one block) - this causes format errors. Submit with 'echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT' as a standalone action only when you have evidence of a real fix.
hints: This is a multi-repo benchmark with diverse project structures - always start by identifying the repo layout with ls or find before searching. Use grep with specific patterns (error messages, function names) rather than broad searches that produce too much output. When editing, NEVER use broad sed patterns like 's/old/new/g' across an entire file without line number restrictions - always constrain edits to specific verified line ranges (e.g., '10,12s/old/new/g'). If output exceeds 10000 characters you'll only see head/tail - use more selective commands (head, tail, sed -n) or redirect to a file and search within it. On macOS systems, use 'sed -i ""' instead of 'sed -i'. The test command varies by repo (pytest, python -m unittest, repo-specific scripts) - look for test files or CI configs to identify the correct command. Directory and environment changes don't persist across commands - prefix with 'cd /path && ...' if needed.
budget_guidance: Allocate roughly 3-4 steps to LOCATE (finding the buggy file), 5-7 steps to UNDERSTAND (reading and identifying exact lines), and the remaining 25-30 steps to FIX (editing, verifying, testing, iterating). Do NOT spend more than 7-8 steps total before making your first edit - open-ended exploration is the primary cause of timeout failures. If you exceed 25 steps total, immediately prioritize completing a fix attempt over gathering more information. If stuck after 3-4 failed attempts at the same approach, switch strategies rather than repeating. Reserve at least 5-10 steps for verification and iteration after your first edit - fixes rarely work on the first try. On issues that appear simple (single file, clear error message), compress LOCATE to 1-2 steps and UNDERSTAND to 3-4 steps to leave more budget for careful fixing and testing.
